reasons: The production gate is a safe default, but only one setting controls it.

terms.meaning: A value set outside the code, such as whether the app runs in production.
Whether search engines list a page in their results.
A small label showing one of the app's named personality types.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the gallery
sections.what: Brings in the page type, the not-found helper, the settings reader, the display pieces, the persona list and the ticket demo.
sections.why: Needed to draw each gallery block.

sections.name: metadata
sections.title: Page settings
sections.what: Sets the tab title, asks search engines not to list the page, and forces the page to build fresh on each visit.
sections.why: Likely reason: a development page should not be indexed or stored as a static copy.
sections.watch_out: Removing the no-index flag could let search engines find the gallery if it is turned on.

sections.name: EXAMPLE
sections.title: Example receipt values
sections.what: Holds a fixed example source with a verified-delayed class and a fixed date, used by the receipt sample.
sections.why: The code comment says gallery examples are illustrative and point to example, not real data.
sections.watch_out: Keep the source id as example so a real receipt is never mistaken for sample data.

sections.name: Section
sections.title: Gallery block wrapper
sections.what: A small wrapper that draws a titled block with an id and a test label for each component.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps every gallery block looking the same.
sections.watch_out: The id is used for both the heading link and the test label, so duplicates would clash.

sections.name: DesignGallery
sections.title: Gallery page
sections.what: Checks the environment, then draws the header and a block for each shared component with illustrative values.
sections.why: Likely reason: one page lets the developer review every component.
sections.watch_out: The production gate is the only protection, so DESIGN_GALLERY must stay off in production.

summary: A development gallery that shows every shared display component with sample values, hidden in production unless a setting turns it on.
purpose: Lets the developer check how the shared visual pieces look and behave in one place.
why: Likely reason: it is a development tool, and the production gate keeps it out of the public site.
how: Checks the environment first. In production it shows Not Found unless the DESIGN_GALLERY setting is on. Otherwise it draws a header and one section per component with sample data, and asks search engines not to index the page.
inputs: Environment settings including NODE_ENV and DESIGN_GALLERY, plus sample values inside the file.
outputs: A page with sections for the ticket, stamps, receipt, meter, seismograph, timing tower row, persona chips, status badges and share card.
risks: If DESIGN_GALLERY is set in production, the gallery becomes visible. Sample names such as Example fan look like real data.
debug: If the gallery shows Not Found, check NODE_ENV and DESIGN_GALLERY. If one component looks broken, check its own file and the sample props here.
